findings.location: Translation — many places contain embedded NUL/escape sequences (e.g. "\u0000e0", "\u0000e2", "\u0000f4", etc.)
findings.source_quote: Example from source: "As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve..." (normal text with standard punctuation and accents only in English source)
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the encoding escape sequences and restore normal French characters. For example, replace sequences like "\u0000e0" by 'à', "\u0000e9" by 'é', "\u0000e8" by 'è', "\u0000e2" by 'â', "\u0000f4" by 'ô', "\u0000e7" by 'ç', and fix stray NUL bytes. Ensure the string encoding is UTF-8 and that no '\u0000' tokens remain in the translated HTML text. Keep HTML tags exactly as in the translation file.
findings.translation_quote: Car l\u0000epoux incr\u0000e9dule est sanctifi\u0000e9 par la femme... (numerous occurrences throughout the translated HTML)

findings.location: Translation — proper names and words corrupted or mistranslated (within paragraph about Eunice and Lois; also earlier: "vessels" -> "v�eases saints")
findings.source_quote: "Eunice was a Jewess... We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois..." and earlier: "They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy."
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the proper names and key nouns in correct French forms and spelling, preserving HTML. Replace 'blemish' with 'tache' or the conventional French biblical phrasing 'sans tache ni ride' as in standard French Bible renderings. Preserve the blockquote and <em> tags and the verse reference unchanged.

findings.location: Translation — paragraph-level mistranslation/awkwardness: sentence about Eunice not circumcising her son (meaning changed/confusing)
findings.source_quote: "This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer."
